about: The area map: which named product area owns which source paths. It answers five questions, each for a machine: (1) given a path, which one area owns it; (2) given an area, which path globs it owns; (3) given two planned issues, do their areas overlap, where overlap means a shared area or either touching `shared`; (4) which `area:<name>` issue label an area corresponds to; (5) which files match no area. Globs must not overlap: a file matches exactly one area, in any order; `**` spans directories, `*` does not. `test/areas-map.test.js` enforces that every file under server.js, lib/, public/ and scripts/ matches exactly one area, that every glob matches a file, and that an area with no paths yet is one `shared.holds` still names. `shared` is the two files still holding several areas; each extraction (#2248) moves one family out and removes it from `shared.holds`. Tests are mapped by the module they test and are deliberately outside the totality check.

kernel.label: area:kernel
kernel.why: The HTTP route table, matcher, responders and body parser every route module shares, and the caller-identity proofs several families share; owned by no one family.

store.label: area:store
store.why: The database handle every store module shares, and the schema with its one ordered migration chain; owned by no one domain.

activity.label: area:activity
activity.why: The activity log: the event trail the dashboard shows and its per-type retention.

audit.label: area:audit
audit.why: Eval audit mode (ingest, scoring, incidents, retention), OpenClaw process visibility, and the local project scorecard cache plus its producer (#1949, #2144).

wrap.label: area:wrap
wrap.why: The session wrap pipeline, its steps, the changelog fragments it compiles and release readiness.

openclaw.label: area:openclaw
openclaw.why: OpenClaw connections, tunnels, the direct and view proxies.

bridge.label: area:discord-bridge
bridge.why: The operator bridge: Discord relay, the Project Master's structured surface, candidates and routes.

medusa.label: area:medusa
medusa.why: The switchboard: inbox, exchanges, deliveries, wake and watchdog.

control.label: area:control
control.why: Durable HOLD/RELEASE/STOP, the merge queue, check watches, scoped permission requests, and durable interactive decision requests.

launch.label: area:launch
launch.why: Session launch: sequences, preflight, recovery, startup prompt and control, handoffs, rotations and the prime.

session-rules.label: area:session-rules
session-rules.why: Operator-authored session rules, their delivery and refresh, and learnings.

sessions.label: area:sessions
sessions.why: Session lifecycle in tmux and ttyd, the Project Master, transcripts, continuity, workload receipts, engine error watching, and host-level causes of an apparently-idle session (#1112: a blocking macOS GUI dialog no pane capture can see).

auth.label: area:auth
auth.why: Operator accounts, sign-in, recovery codes, service and install tokens, the gates and fallback.

setup.label: area:setup
setup.why: Install and ingress: HTTPS setup, certificates, Caddy, provisioning, host and port scanning. `lib/host-check.js`/`lib/host-inventory.js` named explicitly, not by a `lib/host-*.js` glob: #1112 (`sessions` area) added `lib/host-gui-dialog-probe.js`, a different sense of "host" (the macOS desktop, not network/ingress host scanning) that glob would otherwise also catch.

projects.label: area:projects
projects.why: Project records, config, paths and versions, generated files, git hooks and templates, plan docs and actions, and the cross-project version dependency registry (#777).

engines.label: area:engines
engines.why: Engine definitions, models, temp roots, profiles, engine error detection, and the shared compatibility canary and capability-matched admission gate (#1897, #1809) every adapter resolves exact-build state through.

shared-docs.label: area:shared-docs
shared-docs.why: Cross-project shared documents, groups, locks, events and notices.

update.label: area:update-checker
update.why: Update checking and applying, and the upstream observer.

checkouts.label: area:checkouts
checkouts.why: Checkout state, freshness and fleet, git probes, GitHub facts and checks, CI status and branch retirement.

system.label: area:system
system.why: Host and process facts: system info and health, server info, governance state, the logger.

tc.label: area:tc
tc.why: The `tc` command line. `lib/tc-docs-scorecard-merge-wiring.js` (#2887, #2878, #2883, #2877, Ruling A502-W1C-R2) is this area's library/verb adapter surface: it composes `docs-manual`'s, `merge-governance`'s, `audit`'s (scorecard) and `roadmap`'s own self-contained libraries into the call shapes a `tc` verb (or a future route) needs, without those libraries themselves living here.

tooling.label: area:tooling
tooling.why: Repository scripts, release certification, soak harnesses, the Vercel build guard and the docs/screenshot parity signal.

config.label: area:config
config.why: The global config routes: the settings read and save, with the secret redaction, bind state, protected roots and Master-settings validation they carry.

external-code-security.label: area:external-code-security
external-code-security.why: The untrusted-PR review boundary (#1554): sanitizing and non-executably fencing untrusted external PR text, and checking a review session's declared capabilities against the read-only review contract ADR 0014 requires. Owned by no other family; docs/external-code-security.md is the full write-up.

fleet-provisioning.label: area:fleet-provisioning
fleet-provisioning.why: Idempotent Fleet Group, shared LANE_QUEUE doc and Merge Queue bootstrap for a newly stood-up fleet or strike team (#2825, Ruling A2825) -- a real orchestration function over store.projectGroups/store.sharedDocs and (authority permitting) the Merge Queue, unlike this wave's other pure Slice 1 libraries. Owned by no other family.

fleet-views.label: area:fleet-views
fleet-views.why: Fleet and dashboard view projections for the landing page and Master fleet view (#349, #1923), opt-in switchboard auto-inject gating and swarm stats (#801), a visible project-version-cache write-failure diagnostic (#1046), and recorded test-suite duration stats (#1784) -- the `v5.60.0 Fleet and dashboard views` milestone's own Car 60-C. Distinct from `sessions`' `lib/workload*.js` (asserted lane availability for dispatch) and `medusa`'s `lib/medusa*.js` (the switchboard engine itself): these are read-only projections over already-fetched facts from both, built for display rather than dispatch. Owned by no other family. `lib/fleet-visibility-routes.js` (#2858, Ruling A503-R1, Car 66-C) is the Slice 2 route adapter this area's own text already named as a tracked follow-up: composed controller functions over all four libraries here, ready for Milestone #54's real route mount.

terminal-chrome.label: area:terminal-chrome
terminal-chrome.why: Deterministic per-project visual identity for terminal views (#1573) and multi-file upload queue state with auto-appending Attachment Pills (#1577) -- the `v5.60.0 Fleet and dashboard views` milestone's Car 60-D pure libraries feeding the composer/terminal chrome. Distinct from `lib/uploads*.js` (`sessions` area: the real filesystem upload path these pill states will eventually drive) and from `dashboard-ux` (`public/**`, the DOM these feed): these are pure derivation/queue logic, not I/O or rendering. Owned by no other family; Slice 2 wiring into routes/UI is a tracked follow-up.

resource-leases.label: area:resource-leases
resource-leases.why: Runtime-enforced Resource Module leases and safe transitions (#2014), plus delegated-authority provision/retire of resource modules (#2071) — a pure state machine, co-hosted per Architect Rulings A2014/A2071's shared file envelope. Owned by no other family. `lib/resource-lease-routes.js` (#2856, Ruling A503-R1, Car 66-C) is the Slice 2 route adapter: composed handlers over this module plus `role-instruction-guard`'s own evaluator (the delegation/outbound-instruction angle #2856 bundles with the lease state machine), ready for Milestone #54's real route mount.

role-instruction-guard.label: area:role-instruction-guard
role-instruction-guard.why: The role-instruction mismatch classifier and confirmation gate (#2397, Ruling A2397): a pure detector deciding whether an outbound instruction looks sent to the wrong role. Owned by no other family; Slice 2 wiring into dispatch routes/composer UI is a tracked follow-up.

merge-governance.label: area:merge-governance
merge-governance.why: Who may merge and whether a merge may proceed. The cross-engine Builder `gh pr merge` role guard (#2601, Ruling A2601): a pure classifier/evaluator deciding whether a candidate shell command is a PR-merge invocation, and whether the caller's role/lane is authorized to run it under Rule #282. The durable action-scoped merge constraint / hold engine (#1717 Slice 1, Ruling A500-W1B-R1): persists holds against a stable repo+PR/branch/issue identity, independent of any session's Medusa inbox, and gates merge/auto-merge/release/restart on them. Owned by no other family; wiring either into a real launch-env wrapper, engine shell hook, live route, or GitHub status check is a tracked Slice 2 follow-up (#2878).

roadmap.label: area:roadmap
roadmap.why: Roadmap train dependency admission and incremental GitHub roadmap-sync state (#1894, #2259) — logic for the separate, Builder-read-only roadmap-board repository (ADR 0024) to adopt, not a replacement for it. Owned by no other family. Named explicitly, not by glob: `lib/roadmap-*.js` also matched `lib/roadmap-vercel-guard.js` once #2258 added it under `tooling`.

docs-manual.label: area:docs-manual
docs-manual.why: The indexable, dual-audience (human/NHE) product manual and the repo-wide AI documentation router (#811, #2835, Slice 2 of #2070) — parity-checkable manifests over the narrative docs. Owned by no other family. Named explicitly, not by glob, learning from the `roadmap` area's own collision.

linux-systemd.label: area:linux-systemd
linux-systemd.why: The Linux half of background service management (#1424): a systemd user-unit generator, install/uninstall/status orchestration over systemctl --user / loginctl, and the restart-button contract verifier. The macOS half (launchd plists) stays in scripts/ingress-cutover.js and is not reassigned here. Owned by no other family.

sprint-tracking.label: area:sprint-tracking
sprint-tracking.why: Native sprint wave tracking (#2644, Car 68-A, Train 35): wave-matrix and file-disjoint car bundle validation, the live lane/PR dispatch-state tracker, the interactive sprint report/O-Gate summary model, the resilient roadmap sync helper, and its thin not-yet-mounted HTTP adapter. `public/sprint-wave-ui.js`'s browser view helpers are not listed here: `dashboard-ux`'s `public/**` already owns every file under `public/`. Distinct from `roadmap` (train dependency admission over the separate roadmap-board repo) and `fleet-views` (read-only dashboard projections, not dispatch state): this area models the wave/car/lane/PR lifecycle itself. Owned by no other family.

shared.why: Files still holding several areas; an issue touching one overlaps with every area it holds until it is empty.
